messages.subject: MSstatsPTM progenesis questions
parts:
Dear all,

I am someone rather new to (phospho)proteomics analysis and have recently been handed a dataset at my new job where they asked me to assist with the analysis of a mouse dataset. I managed the proteomics portion fine (the MSstats guide is really good!) but I’m struggling with the PTM part and was hoping I could get some feedback here.

For the PTM part they did a peptide-level phospho-enrichment, measuring in DDA mode. Then they did a progenesis aligment and mascot search.

I now have ther progenesis-style output, but there are several elements where I’m not sure if they could be a problem (the MSstatsPTM guide that I found did not have much info regarding expected Progenesis input):

1) I have an extra column that is mostly empty, but which sometimes has 1 (or more) ‘alternative’ Accessions. Is this a problem? Currently I just filter this out.

2) Some rows do not have a PTM. Should I filter these out? What about when there are multiple PTMs?

3) Most Accessions are of the format sp| UniProtID|geneID_MOUSE. However, sometimes I also find things labeled eg. Biognosys|iRT (synthetic peptides for LC-MS standardization?), REV_sp (decoy protein hits?), tr|A8KBU6|A8KBU6_CON-DANRE (Danio Rerio proteins??) and sp|P05783|K1C18_CON-HUMAN (proteins incorrectly labeled as human?). What do I do with these, also just throw them all out?

4) In addition to these questions, after I run ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat I find that I cannot run dataSummarizationPTM due to “Missing columns in the PTM input: PeptideSequence”. However, when I then manually rename the 2nd column from 'PeptideModifiedSequence' to 'PeptideSequence', it does work. Is this intended?

5) Finally, I have the data from the regular proteomics experiment they did and was hoping to integrate this into the PTM analysis (indeed, this is why I was so keen to try MSstatsPTM in the first place, the paper convinced me it was worth it to invest the effort). However, for this experiment the measurement was in DIA mode and the output I got was from Spectronaut. Since the ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat function expects the global_protein_input to also be in Progenesis format, is there a way I can still integrate these two datasets? Perhaps by using the MSstats SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat output and adding this to the ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat output somehow?

 

That was a lot, but if any of you can give me some advice or pointers to help me get the analysis correct, it would be greatly appreciated!

Please find in attach some example screenshots to help illustrate these questions. 


Kind regards,

Robin Colpaert

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: MSstatsPTM progenesis questions
parts:
Hi Robin,

Apologies for the delayed response. I will address your points in order below. I do want to say off that the Progenesis converter is an older converter and it is possible that there are issues we will need to address.

1) I am assuming this second column is for peptides that were not uniquely identified as belonging to one protein. In this case the other protein is listed in the second column. These rows can be kept or removed based on if you want to use these non-unique ids.

2) You can safely filter out rows without a PTM. In terms of multiple PTMs, MSstatsPTM should keep these, but summarize these separately from single modified peptides.

3) These should be filtered out.

4) I think this is due to Progenesis is an old converter and you are totally fine updating the columns in this way.

5) This is possible, but will require a bit of manual work. What you need to do is run the proteome data separately with the MSstats converter, and then add it into the MSstatsPTM workflow. I have included a quick script to do this below.

```
library(MSstatsPTM)
library(MSstats)

MSstatsPTM_input = ProgenesistoMSstatsPTMFormat(ptm_data, annotation_file)

MSstats_input = SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(protein_data, protein_annotation_file)

MSstatsPTM_input$PROTEIN = MSstats_input

summarized_data = dataSummarizationPTM(MSstatsPTM_input)
```

I hope this makes sense. Feel free to follow up with any additional questions/clarifications.

Devon
